newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Sept 25.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Sept 25.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN
A call up to Australia's overseas-based stars will go out from national soccer coach Eddie Thomson for the Socceroos' one-off match against Saudi Arabia next month. Page 21.

North Melbourne's ruckman Corey McKernan did not see any reason to change the AFL rules for receiving a Brownlow Medal, even though he missed out on a medal this year because he was suspended. Page 22.
St George has targeted Manly's Matthew Ridge for harsh treatment in their next meeting in the Australian Rugby League grand final, as Ridge was concussed in his last game. Page 22.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD
The Sydney Swans' Andrew Dunkley may still miss the AFL grand final if the charge over an incident involving Brownlow Medal winner James Hird is not settled soon. Page 52.

Controversy still surrounds comments from the Manly side against Cronulla fullback David Peachey last weekend, with St George captain Mark Coyne stating that Manly's coach Bob Fulton encourages his players to sledge their opponents. Page 52.

Suffering pain in his right ring finger after three limited-over games for the Victorian squad in Darwin, Shane Warne is increasingly hesitant about undertaking a position on the Australian cricket team's tour of India next month. Page 52. --
THE AGE

The call for change to the AFL's Brownlow Medal rules has been challenged by the first man to miss out on contention through suspension - Corey McKernan said that he saw no reason to change the rules. Page C12.

With the AFL's investigation into the incident involving Andrew Dunkley taking up its third day, Sydney Swans coach Rodney Eade has slammed the AFL for taking too long, claiming the distraction could cost the Swans their competitive edge in Saturday's grad final. Page C12.

Following strong performances overseas, including Rodney McGee's and Nathan O'Neill's finishes in the top three in the under-23 section of the Grand Prix des Nations in France and Peter Rogers' third in Germany's Hesen tour, Australian road cyclists have raised hopes of a good performance in next month's Commonwealth Bank Classic. Page C9.
HERALD SUN
Wayne Jackson is expected next month to take on the top job in Australian football, replacing Ross Oakley. Oakley will be stepping down after serving as the AFL chief for 10 years. Page 80.

The AFL has banned Optus Vision from airing new footage of the incident between James Hird and Andrew Dunkley which occurred in last week's preliminary final and saw Hird leave the field after a tackle by Dunkley. Page 80.
Driver Larry Perkins has chosen not to race in his VR Commodore and will instead race at Mount Panorama in a fortnight in a superseded VP-series Holden V8. Page 73.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH
The St George team has come up with a plan on its retreat near Moss Vale to beat Manly's fierce defensive game, a defence which kept Cronulla pointless last week. Page 72.

Olympic beach volleyballer Liane Fenwick, who with her current teammate is ranked ninth in the world, will be seeking a new teammate for the Australian circuit this summer following her Olympic partner Anita Spring's retirement. Page 70.

Basketball's version of the Super League has produced an extra 30 new names on the NBL's free agent list for next season, but unfortunately, over half of the 30 players from the soon-to-be defunct Hobart Devils, Geelong Supercats and Gold Coast Rollers will find it hard to make a State league team, let alone an NBL side. Page 64.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
